title: Eventual detection of zero in affine etale cohomology
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set and let $D:I^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Sch}$ be an inverse diagram of affine quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms. Let $(X,(f_i))$ be a limit cone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For each $i$, let $F_i$ be an abelian sheaf on $(D_i)_{\acute{e}t}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with maps $\varphi_f:D(f^{\mathrm{op}})^{-1}F_i\to F_j$ for $f:i\to j$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] satisfying the canonical inverse-image identity and composition laws. Let $G:I\to\operatorname{Ab}(X_{\acute{e}t})$ be identified objectwise with $f_i^{-1}F_i$ by isomorphisms, its arrows being inverse-image composition followed by pullback of $\varphi_f$. Let $L$ be a colimit cocone on $G$, with coprojections $\iota_i$. Fix $p\ge0$. Write $eG_i:G_i\cong f_i^{-1}F_i$ for the specified isomorphisms. For every $i\in I$ and $x\in H^p(D_i,F_i)$ whose image $H^p(\iota_i\circ eG_i^{-1})(f_i^*x)$ is zero in $H^p(X,L)$, there exist $j\in I$ and $f:i\to j$ such that $H^p(\varphi_f)(D(f^{\mathrm{op}})^*x)=0$. This asserts eventual detection of zero only, with no assertion that all limit classes descend.

proof.text: Induct on p, generalizing the coefficient system F, its transition maps, the limit coefficient diagram and colimit cocone, and the initial stage i. In degree zero apply etale_limit_affine_degree_zero_kernel directly to x and its zero limit image.

In successor degree n+1 apply etale_limit_affine_corrected_lift. It supplies a compatible coefficient system R with limit diagram T and colimit K, additive connecting maps delta natural for transitions, and a later stage j with transition f and a degree-n class z. The limit image of z is zero, and delta_j(z) is the f-transition of x.

Apply the degree-n induction hypothesis to R, T, K and z at j. Obtain a later stage k and transition g killing z. Naturality of delta and its additivity show that the g-transition of delta_j(z) is zero. Substitute the corrected-lift identity to conclude that the consecutive f- and g-transitions kill x.

Use cohomologyMap_map and the explicit composition comparison cohomologyMap_comp_explicit, proved from the composition clause of cohomologyPullbackFunctorial, to identify successive pullbacks. Rewrite by the given coefficient composition law hcomposition and Sheaf.H.map_comp_apply. The consecutive transitions are precisely the transition along f composed with g, which gives the required witness k.
